subject: Request: SLA carve-out for customer-managed colo and downstream WAN

Subject: Request: SLA carve-out for customer-managed colo and downstream WAN

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — we appreciated the performance profiles you shared. As we move toward procurement and legal review, our architecture team surfaced a set of dependencies we need to formalize in contract language: EdgeCorp will be hosting a private colo that contains our Key Management Service (KMS) and an active BGP handoff to our WAN provider. The colo and the upstream WAN are entirely under our operational control.

Specifically we need Redwood to acknowledge a carve-out in uptime/latency responsibilities for any incidents where the root cause is inside our colo or on our downstream WAN (including transit provider maintenance, BGP flap, or private circuit issues). For procurement, legal has asked for: 1) the exact wording you propose for a "customer-controlled infra" exception, 2) a list of evidence artifacts Redwood requires to attribute an incident, and 3) an end-to-end incident example that shows attribution steps.

Attached are a network diagram and a short BGP runbook to give context. We're targeting a signed agreement by the end of June, so an expedited review would be appreciated. Can we also schedule a 30-minute call next week with SRE and Legal to walk the draft language?

Attachments: EdgeCorp_Network_Diagram.pdf (pdf), BGP-runbook.txt (txt)

Thanks,
Claire Novak
Head of Infrastructure, EdgeCorp

Claire — really appreciate the context and the attachments. We're happy to work through a limited carve-out for customer-controlled infrastructure, but there are a few operational details we'll need to lock down before Legal will sign off. High level next steps from our side: 

- Vanessa (legal/ops) will draft proposed contract language for a carve-out that limits Redwood's uptime/latency liability to incidents where we can demonstrate root cause is outside Redwood infrastructure.
- Jonas (SRE) will enumerate the telemetry and evidence we require (packet captures, NetFlow/traceroutes, BGP dumps, timestamps) and propose a troubleshooting playbook for attribution.
- I'll coordinate a 30-minute call next Tue or Wed — are you available 10–11am PT on Tue (6/1) or 2–3pm PT on Wed (6/2)?

For the call please have a network engineer and a procurement/legal rep join. In the meantime, Vanessa — can you draft a first-pass clause and attach any precedents we use internally? Jonas — please list the minimal set of data we can accept for a timely attribution review.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite once Claire confirms a slot.

—Chloe

On Fri, May 29, 2026 at 10:05 AM Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Claire — really appreciate the context and the attachments. We're happy to work through a limited carve-out for customer-controlled infrastructure...

Claire / team — attaching a draft clause and an evidence matrix for your review (proposed_sla_carveout_redwood.docx). Summary of the proposal: 

- Narrow carve-out language: Redwood's availability and latency obligations for Private deployments shall not apply to incidents where the root cause is within Customer-controlled colocation facilities, circuits, or downstream transit providers, provided Customer supplies the evidence set described below within 72 hours of request.
- Evidence required (minimal set): BGP RIB/adj-rib-out at time of incident, traceroutes from both ends with timestamps, NetFlow summary for the implicated time window, router/syslog excerpts, and a signed maintenance notice if a scheduled change occurred.
- Attribution timeline: Redwood will perform initial analysis within 24 hours of receiving the evidence and provide a preliminary attribution statement within 72 hours. If additional data is required, we will escalate with a list of items and expected turnaround.
- Suggested contractual wording for procurement (single paragraph): "Where Customer hosts networking, KMS, or connectivity infrastructure outside Redwood's managed environment, Redwood's Service Level Objectives shall exclude periods of unavailability or latency attributable to such Customer-controlled infrastructure where Customer provides the evidence set required for attribution within the timeframe specified in this Agreement."

A few additional notes: we should limit the carve-out to the surface area clearly under customer control (physical colo, customer-managed KMS, and customer-owned interconnect). We cannot accept an open-ended carve-out for third-party SaaS dependencies without further controls. Jonas — please see the attached list of telemetry types that allow attribution; focus on the minimum that still permits a reasonable forensics timeline.

Attachments: proposed_sla_carveout_redwood.docx

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Operations & Contracts, Redwood Inference
